prior_summary: History-informed, phase-conditioned action diffusion with separate arm and gripper epsilon heads. A binary clean-gripper auxiliary, weak ordered event supervision, masked persistence losses and an action-conditioned measured-response predictor distinguish persistent grip events from smooth absolute joint setpoints. The fixed Gaussian DDPM is retained; categorical gripper diffusion is adapted to a Bernoulli auxiliary and binary-support consistency, not represented as an implemented categorical sampler.
applicable_conditions: State-based world-frame unstack_sort under the supplied 20 Hz Panda pd_joint_pos interface. Learn the complete expanded red and blue slices, including open approach, closing, lift, transport, descent, opening, retreat, red-to-blue approach and blue terminal hold. Two causal observations provide qpos, qvel, TCP and both object poses and goals. The implementation infers object role from those observations under the demonstrated red-then-blue ordering; its forward interface has no persistent target-tag or previous-command input.
termination_guidance: Do not initialize this policy to carry or terminate from a place timer. Continue during unfinished closure, transport, descent or measured finger-opening lag. After red release, transfer during compatible open retreat/blue-approach overlap while passing the same observation history, or continue the learned red-to-blue return. After blue, the data support open retreat toward TCP z about 0.300 m and settling. These physical handoff cues do not add requirements to task success, which is only the supplied rotated-containment and center-z predicate for both blocks.
limitations: No categorical corruption kernel, hard binary decoder, persistent recurrent state, command-history input, invocation target input, calibrated phase confidence, explicit duration distribution, IK, FK, contact sensing, safety projection or recovery controller is implemented. The output remains continuous normalized 8D epsilon for the fixed sampler; binary persistence is a learned preference, not a guarantee. Semantic phase labels are weak geometric/motion proxies and successful traces confound event duration with state. The response network is a training-only local predictor, not a verified simulator. No performance result is available at design time.

config.architecture: Two-frame GRUCell history encoder, causal horizon phase predictor, public conditional U-Net for seven arm epsilon coordinates, separate dilated temporal gripper epsilon/Bernoulli branch, training-only response MLP
config.normalization: Unchanged full-original-demonstration shared normalizer; no per-skill fitting or observation clipping
config.segmentation: All 24 assigned expanded segments, unchanged; padding never crosses a slice
phase_order: blue approach including return from red
config.binary_adaptation: Separate continuous gripper epsilon head, jointly trained clean Bernoulli event head, confidence-weighted clean-estimate consistency and binary-support loss; fixed Gaussian DDPM output decoding unchanged
config.phase_supervision: Training-only weak labels from commands, pre/post TCP/object states and pad relations, with 0.04 uniform label smoothing; no timestamps or source indices
config.duration_adaptation: Weak adjacent forward-or-stay posterior penalty and stable-command three-slot curvature penalty; no fixed dwell timer or explicit semi-Markov duration model
config.auxiliary_noise_weight: alpha_bar multiplies clean-estimate auxiliary losses; response and delta auxiliaries clip only their local clean inputs to [-2,2]
config.response_prediction: Seven next measured arm-joint displacements and two next measured finger positions, using complete-data observation scales; displacement task multiplier 16
config.fixed_recipe: DDPM epsilon prediction, 100 train/inference steps, clip_sample true, AdamW 1e-4 with 1e-6 weight decay, cosine schedule with 500 warmup updates, max gradient norm 1, EMA 0.999; supplied U-Net widths 128/256/512, embedding 128, kernel 5, groups 8
